function: GNN maps received uplink pilots directly to the downlink digital precoder, then split into baseband and holographic beamformers, maximizing sum rate without explicit channel estimation (p. 5, 8).
system: Downlink multi-user holographic MIMO: BS surface of M=64 elements at lambda/4 spacing, K=5 (default) single-antenna users, 30 GHz mmWave; surface is the BS aperture, no RIS (p. 4, 10).
method: Graph neural network, two message-passing layers with max-pooling aggregation and fully connected combine, trained unsupervised with the sum-rate loss offline using Adam; no federated, reinforcement or meta-learning (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician fading (kappa 10 dB), LoS from user positions, sinc-correlated NLoS; 10,000 samples split 6000/2000/2000 for training/validation/test; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data (p. 9-10).
test_conditions: Default: same settings for training and testing. Generalization: trained at SNR 10 or 20 dB, tested over SNRs; trained with K=5, tested with other user counts (p. 12).
baselines: Classical: perfect CSI plus WMMSE, MMSE plus WMMSE, LS plus WMMSE, perfect CSI plus SVD. Learned: DNN, the same architecture without message passing (p. 10).
metrics: Sum rate in bps/Hz versus propagation attenuation, antenna spacing, pilot length, frame length, number of antennas, SNR, number of users, and training epochs (p. 11-13).
q1_support: p. 9: "the channel hk is Rician"; custom simulator with sinc-correlated NLoS (p. 9-10), and no 3GPP TR 38.901, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "train other GNN and DNN models using K = 5 and evaluate" their performance across varying numbers of users (Fig. 12), so other user counts than in training.
q3_support: p. 10: "the message-passing process in the updating layer is removed"; Benchmark 4 DNN is the GNN without a module (ablation), the other four benchmarks are non-learned, and no earlier published learned beamformer is compared.
q4_support: p. 10: "reduces the model complexity"; qualitative only. Table III reports sum rate for 2 to 4 layers and Table IV lists layer sizes, with no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime.
q5_support: p. 10: "10,000 samples are divided into 6000, 2000, 2000"; the data are the authors' own simulation, with no link or DOI for code or data and no public dataset.
notes: The HMIMO surface is the BS transmit aperture (reconfigurable holographic surface), not a RIS between BS and users, so ris=0 (p. 4-5); reviewer to confirm. Borderline q3: Benchmark 4 DNN (p. 10) is described as the GNN with message passing removed, treated as an ablation; if the reviewer reads it as a standard fully connected baseline, q3 would be 1. q4: Table IV (p. 10) gives layer sizes only. Area 3: the main metric is sum rate, and implicit channel estimation is part of the same pilot-to-beamformer mapping (p. 5).
